headline: Chinese hospitals are building their own medical AI models and moving them into everyday clinical work, China Daily reports, though doctors still make the final call.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered to 4: the matching China Daily feature is dated 9 Oct 2026, before the window, and the Borneo Bulletin copy could not be opened to confirm it is the same text.
importance_line: Patients and doctors in Chinese hospitals are affected as AI moves from trials into routine care, but the usage and time-saving figures come from the hospitals themselves and data sharing, safety checks and accountability are still open questions.
summary: China Daily reported on 9 Oct 2026 that Chinese hospitals are developing their own medical AI models, such as Med-Go at Shanghai's East Hospital, now used in 46 community health centres and more than 30 hospitals, and Huaxi Hongyi at West China Hospital, whose paperwork agent generated more than 1.1 million medical records in 2025, according to the hospital. It also reports obstacles such as slow responses, fragmented data and privacy concerns, and says the doctor keeps the final say when the AI disagrees.
